title: Count weights raised two harebell width interaction indices in a 2021 North Wales experiment
abstract: We tested how seasonal count weights change a harebell flower-width index in a public ozone and warming experiment. We used 24 released count and width pairs from six chambers and four months in North Wales in 2021. Count weights raised the 80 versus 30 ppb interaction index from 0.3875 to 1.2657 mm, and the 110 versus 30 ppb index from 0.9856 to 1.0942 mm. Both weighted indices stayed positive after every single-month omission. An exact covariance split gives weight contributions of 0.8782 and 0.1086 mm. The latter changes sign when August is omitted. Sharp independent count-error bounds first permit zero at factors of 1.2594 and 1.2258, with widths held fixed. These are assumed error thresholds, not measured errors or confidence limits. Unknown count aggregation, selected flowers, four visits and one chamber per treatment prevent pooled-flower and causal interpretations. This extends prior campaign work with the same source records; it is not independent regional or temporal validation. The package gives original code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and independent linear-program checks. External source records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Equal-month and count-weighted width interaction indices, and sharp count-only error bounds. One chamber per treatment; these are descriptive indices.
